open.description: The bounded streamer slices a JavaScript string by UTF-16 code units. If the 1,200-unit boundary falls between the two code units of a non-BMP character, the first frame contains a lone high surrogate and the next contains a lone low surrogate; JSON transport/downstream storage can corrupt or reject the reply. For example, 'x'.repeat(1199) + '😀' is split at that boundary. Chunk by Unicode code points (or otherwise avoid splitting surrogate pairs) and add a regression test for an astral character at the boundary.

GitHub's authoritative mergeable_state is dirty. The target and this PR both modify backend/testing/__fixtures__/websocket_event_inventory_v1.json, including the inventory entry and the summary counts; resolve that conflict while retaining both sides' intended changes before merge.

resolved.reason: The delta adds failed/abandoned terminal context frames, removes matching ephemeral previews in useConversation, and emits abandonment cleanup before the claim-abandon API in both warm and cold Fast paths.
The streamer now emits 1,200-character chunks, the relay rejects larger chunks, projections mark chunks as ephemeral deltas, and the UI merges them locally without canonical refetch.
backend/testing/test_agent.py now covers accepted seq-0/seq-1 relay selection plus rejection for a stale session and missing/lost claim authority.

issues.description: A preview is emitted in the streamer finally/close path on every exit, including provider failure, claim loss, and abandonment, but the UI has no clear/tombstone path for an ephemeral preview. useConversation merges the preview into local state and every canonical refresh merges server rows into the existing array, so a failed Fast turn's preview remains visible indefinitely until the project/component is reset; it is not persisted and therefore can never be replaced by a durable reply. Add an explicit failed/abandoned preview removal signal or make refresh prune previews that no longer have an active turn.

The relay accepts cumulative content up to 20,000 characters, but message_event_payload applies the 16 KiB websocket budget and marks oversized projections canonical_refetch_required. The UI then skips the realtime merge and fetches the preview UUID from the durable conversation endpoint; that UUID is intentionally never persisted, so the fetch returns nothing and the long preview is discarded. A reply near the allowed maximum therefore stops rendering during its final portion. Streaming previews need a bounded transport path that does not require durable refetch, or the backend must enforce a compatible limit before emitting.

There is no backend test covering the new conversation_message_delta relay. In particular, the claim/task/session authorization fence, the message_created versus message_updated selection, and rejection after claim completion/abandonment are untested; the existing added backend test only exercises the pure projection helper. Add focused router/agent-WebSocket coverage for accepted and rejected frames before relying on this path for authenticated operator-visible replies.

review_history.feedback: The restricted-file rules are respected, and the backend/agent/UI identity contract is otherwise aligned. Merge is blocked by the stale-preview lifecycle, the incompatibility between large ephemeral previews and canonical-refetch handling, and missing backend coverage for the new claim-bound relay.

    def _assert_no_leaked_runner_threads(self):
        """Fail the test whose runner loop outlived its own cleanup.
    
        A surviving daemon loop is a whole-process side effect exactly like a
        closed stdio fd: it keeps issuing real ``_post`` calls, so it lands in
        an unrelated LATER test's mock and that test reports the failure. That
        is how ``TestInitialOrchestratorRetry`` came to see ``_post`` called
        twice while passing in isolation — the extra call came from a heartbeat
        thread started ~200 tests earlier by ``TestCredentialPersistence``.
        Because it is order- and timing-dependent, the file passed under
        ``unittest`` and failed under ``pytest``.
    
        This runs AFTER ``_reset_local_runner_test_state`` has set the shutdown
        event and joined each loop, so reaching it means a loop did not honour
        ``_shutdown_event`` within the join budget — a real production defect,
        not test bookkeeping. Checking per-test pins the blame where it belongs
        and is un-gameable: a thread is either alive or it is not.
        """
        leaked = _live_runner_threads()
        if leaked:
            names = ", ".join(sorted(thread.name for thread in leaked))
